Subject: DPA — KMS, rotation, BYOK requirements (initial ask)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking the call yesterday. As discussed, FintechCorp requires a few clarifications and firm commitments in the DPA before our Procurement and Security teams sign off. The key items:

- BYOK / customer-managed keys: we need confirmation of the BYOK flow, whether Redwood supports importing customer keys into an HSM-backed KMS or whether Redwood acts as key custodian;
- Key rotation & access controls: minimum rotation cadence, key access authorization model (RBAC, break-glass, emergency access logs);
- Key escrow / emergency key retrieval: we need an escrow/threshold policy for emergency export if Redwood is unavailable (describe process and time-to-retrieve);
- Subprocessor notifications and approval windows: FintechCorp requires 30 days notice for new subprocessors and the right to review;
- Evidence: sample audit evidence (KMS usage logs, rotation records, HSM attestation) or a playbook showing how Redwood will provide requested artifacts.

Attached is a short redline from Legal capturing our baseline asks (FintechCorp_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). Can you confirm what changes you can accept versus propose alternatives? Also confirm whether you will sign via DocuSign.

Appreciate a response this week — Procurement has a deadline Dec 10.

Best,
Elena Morris
Director, Legal Ops
FintechCorp

Elena —

Thanks for the clear summary and the redline. We can address most of these in the DPA and the TOMs exhibit; below is our proposed approach at a high level. I am attaching our current TOMs exhibit (RW_TOMs_Exhibit_v4.pdf) with inline notes for the items you called out.

1) BYOK / Key custody
   - We support two modes: (A) Customer-managed keys (BYOK) where customers bring keys into a customer-specific HSM backing (recommended for regulated workloads), and (B) Redwood-managed KMS where keys are created and managed by Redwood.
   - For BYOK mode we provide an onboarding handshake: customer uploads an encrypted key blob into an HSM module in your chosen cloud region; Redwood never exports the raw key material.

2) Key rotation & authZ
   - Rotation: default rotation cadence is 365 days; shorter cadences (e.g., 90/180 days) are supported and configurable per-tenant.
   - AuthZ: RBAC enforced via our IAM; access to key material requires dual-approval and is recorded in our audit trail (see section 3.2 in the TOMs).

3) Escrow / emergency retrieval
   - We offer an optional key-escrow workflow: an encrypted escrow copy is stored in a customer-specific bucket encrypted with the customer key; retrieval requires a documented approval process (customer request + Redwood CS and legal approval). Target time to support retrieval is 48–72 hours under normal circumstances; we will document SLA exceptions.

4) Subprocessors
   - We can accept a 30-day notice for new subprocessors and will provide a regular list of subprocessors on the shared Drive link. For high-risk subprocessors (HSM/Key management vendors) we will notify earlier and provide attestation.

5) Evidence and artifacts
   - We can provide exportable KMS usage logs, rotation history, and HSM attestation for the lifecycle window you need (we currently retain KMS telemetry for 2 years by default; retention can be extended under contract).

Action items: Aditya — please confirm commercial flexibility on optional escrow add-on pricing. Neha — can you review the TOMs edits I’ve added and confirm the wording on dual-approval and the retrieval SLA? Elena — I’ve attached a DPA draft that incorporates the above; if acceptable we can produce a DocuSign envelope for execution.

I can be available for a short gap-review call tomorrow if useful.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

(added to Section 5.4 and TOMs Exhibit, section 4.1).

2) Subprocessor notice & objection: We accept 30-day notice for new subprocessors. For subprocessors classified as high-risk (HSM providers, key custodians, forensic vendors) we accept your 10 business day objection window; Redwood will provide attestation and extra detail where requested.

4) BYOK onboarding: confirmed — handshake that imports the customer-encrypted key blob into a customer-specific HSM; Redwood will not export raw key material.
